title: The New Orleans beat and small-group sets at the Saratoga
summary: Russell's rhythm section had a New Orleans beat, and he had the New Orleans players take over as a small band while downtown musicians packed the club.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, now, that rhythm section has been mentioned as maybe one of the greatest rhythm sections in Jazz. How did you feel about the Russell rhythm section? Wasn't that a powerhouse behind you, that made you feel like...?
Oh, it was a very good rhythm section. Very good. Paul Barbarin, you mean?
Mmm-hmm. Well, I mean the whole thing, with Pops, Barbarin, Johnson...

Yeah, and Luis Russell, too. Very good. They had that real Dixie...that real New Orleans beat -- because they were from down there. So Paul and Pops Foster, they knew what they was doin'. And Russell was brought up around there, New Orleans. Yeah, they had that beat all right.
But the kick I used to get out of the band is when
Russell would have them up there as a small band out of a big band, and he'd have all these fellas from New Orleans playing.
Well, there was Red, there would be Higgenbotham in it, and there would be Pops Foster, and there would be Albert Nicholas, and there would be Russell, and I don't know who the other ones...
Oh, they used to do things.
They used to play, and they played the New Orleans numbers. That's the first time I used to hear some of them New Orleans numbers. Man, they could lay it on you, too. Oh! Terrific, terrific.
So this is something that would happen while you were performing? In other words, it would be like...

Russell would tell us, 'Man, lay out' -- you know, get off the stand. And they would take over. They would take over. And it would be something worth listening to. They had the place... They had the Saratoga Club packed at night, like that, with musicians from downtown. What's the name of... Everybody says Benny Goodman was first, I don't know why... But Benny was there

also; he used to come in there. Of course, he wasn't Benny Goodman then. He was just another clarinetist. But Jimmy Dorsey, Tommy Dorsey, Dick McDonough, you name 'em, they were all up there. And they were diggin' that beat; you know, that New Orleans beat that they were puttin' down. Because nobody else was playing it. And they were diggin' it.
Of course, to Russell it didn't mean a thing. Well, that sounded good to me. That's all I wanted to do, was listen at it. I'd get off the stand. That's my paranoia(?). But they would be wailin'.
